content: Custom-made foot orthoses are frequently prescribed for the management of foot pain. The primary objective of this study was to assess the effectiveness of custom-made foot orthoses in treating various types of foot pain. To achieve this, a comprehensive search was conducted across multiple databases, including the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), MEDLINE, EMBASE, CINAHL, and the Physiotherapy Evidence Database (PEDro), covering studies up to June 2007. Additionally, the authors contacted researchers in the field and reviewed reference lists of included trials to identify relevant studies. No restrictions were applied regarding language or publication type. The inclusion criteria for the analysis were randomized controlled trials and controlled clinical trials that evaluated custom-made foot orthoses for any type of foot pain. The outcomes assessed included measurable levels of foot pain, functional ability, disability, health-related quality of life, participant satisfaction, adverse effects, and compliance with the intervention. Two independent reviewers selected the trials, assessed their methodological quality, and cross-checked the extracted data. The data were analyzed separately based on the specific diagnosis of foot pain and the duration of follow-up. A total of 11 trials involving 1,332 participants were included in the review. Among these, five trials focused on custom-made foot orthoses for plantar fasciitis (691 participants), three trials addressed foot pain in rheumatoid arthritis (231 participants), and one trial each examined foot pain in pes cavus (154 participants), hallux valgus (209 participants), and juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) (47 participants). Comparisons were made between custom-made foot orthoses and various other interventions, including sham orthoses, no intervention, standardized interventions provided to all participants, prefabricated (non-custom) foot orthoses, combined manipulation or stretching, night splints, and surgery. The follow-up periods ranged from one week to three years. The findings indicated that custom-made foot orthoses were effective for managing painful pes cavus (number needed to treat for benefit [NNTB]: 5), rearfoot pain in rheumatoid arthritis (NNTB: 4), foot pain in JIA (NNTB: 3), and painful hallux valgus (NNTB: 6). However, for hallux valgus, surgery was found to be even more effective. Additionally, non-custom foot orthoses appeared to be equally effective for JIA, although the analysis may have lacked sufficient statistical power to detect a significant difference. The effectiveness of custom-made foot orthoses for plantar fasciitis and metatarsophalangeal joint pain in rheumatoid arthritis remains unclear. Importantly, custom-made foot orthoses were found to be a safe intervention across all studies. The authors concluded that there is limited evidence to guide clinical decision-making regarding the prescription of custom-made foot orthoses for foot pain. Currently, the strongest evidence (gold level) supports their use for painful pes cavus, while moderate evidence (silver level) supports their use for foot pain associated with JIA, rheumatoid arthritis, plantar fasciitis, and hallux valgus.
